chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the expiation for an oath in His Exalted's saying, 'But whoever cannot find [a camel] - then fasting for three days,' [what is the limit of] 'whoever cannot find'? For indeed a man asks regarding his expiation while he has the means. He said, 'When there is no surplus for him beyond the sustenance of his dependents, he is among those who cannot find.'

key_terms.مَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ: Whoever cannot find (the means to free a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'cannot find' for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the juristic definition of 'cannot find' (la yajid) by anchoring it to the concept of disposable income rather than absolute destitution. He specifies that an individual is considered unable to pay only when they possess no surplus wealth beyond the essential sustenance (qut) of their dependents, a criterion that balances financial feasibility with the seriousness of oath-breaking. This interpretation aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of linking the expiation stages to one's actual economic capacity, ensuring the obligation is neither overly burdensome nor easily evaded.
